info.description:
The Databallr API: NBA and WNBA stats, player and team data, WOWY, shot quality,
and SixRings.

This page lists the operations a personal API key can call.

## Quick start

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DATABALLR_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.databallr.com/v1/nba/standings"
```

## Client libraries

TypeScript and JavaScript: [`@databallr/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@databallr/sdk),
typed from this document. Each operation's code samples show its SDK method.

```bash
npm install @databallr/sdk
```

## Authentication

1. Sign in at https://accounts.databallr.com/account/api-keys. The **API keys** page
   is listed only for accounts with API key access. Create a key, pick its scopes,
   and copy it: the full key is shown once.
2. Send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys start with
   `dbrk_` and work only on `https://api.databallr.com`. Keys that start with
   `dbtk_` are internal and work only on staging.

A key is read-only. Each operation on this page shows the one scope it needs:

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `stats:read` | `GET` under `/v1/nba/` and `/v1/wnba/`, plus the POST queries below |
| `games:read` | `GET` under `/v1/apps/` (SixRings leaderboards, profiles, and stats) |
| `account:read` | `GET` under `/v1/users/me/` (your own favorites, saved views, and settings) |

The POST queries that `stats:read` allows send their query in the JSON body and
change nothing:

  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/enhanced-stats`
  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/lineup/combos`
  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/lineup/players`
  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/lineup/summary`
  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/player-wowy`
  - `POST /v1/nba/pbp/wowy-combos-stats`
  - `POST /v1/nba/teams/similarity`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/enhanced-stats`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/lineup/combos`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/lineup/players`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/lineup/summary`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/player-wowy`
  - `POST /v1/wnba/pbp/wowy-combos-stats`

Every other method is refused, `HEAD` included: use `GET`.

### Errors

Errors use the shared envelope `{"success": false, "error": <code>, "message": <text>}`. Codes are UPPER_SNAKE; the `WWW-Authenticate` challenge keeps the lowercase OAuth names.

These are the codes a key can get on any operation:

| Status | `error` | When | Headers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 | `INVALID_TOKEN` | The key is unknown, expired, revoked, or its account lost API key access. Sent on every path, public reads included. | `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` |
| 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` | The key lacks the operation's scope, or no scope allows the operation (writes, `HEAD`, paths outside this page). | `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="<scope>"`; `scope` is present when a scope would allow it |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | The key is over a budget below, or one address sent too many unrecognized keys. | `Retry-After: 60` |
| 502 | `UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` | The data source behind the operation failed or could not be reached. Safe to retry with backoff. | |

An operation's own errors (bad input, nothing found) carry one code per
status, with the reason in `message` (`"Valid user_id is required"`):

| Status | `error` |
|---|---|
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` |
| 413 | `BODY_TOO_LARGE` |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 502 | `UPSTREAM_ERROR` |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |

Branch on `error` and show `message`, which is written for people and can
change. Some bodies keep extra keys beside these, such as `data` or
`details`.

Responses from this API do not carry the `type` and `retryable` fields
that some databallr game services add to the envelope.

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE",
  "message": "This endpoint needs an API key with the games:read scope."
}
```

### Rate limits

Each key has its own budget, per 60 seconds:

- 120 requests of any kind.
- 20 of the POST queries above. These count toward the 120 too.

Budgets are counted per Cloudflare location and are approximate. Rejected
requests (401, 403) do not count. On a 429, wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

Keys the API has not recently seen as valid are also counted per IP address, 60
per 60 seconds, before they are checked. A client that keeps reusing one valid
key never comes near this.

### Other credentials

First-party apps use credentials a key holder does not need. They appear on
staging operations only.

- **Public session** (`publicSession`): `X-DBR-Session` plus `X-DBR-Client`,
  `X-DBR-Timestamp`, `X-DBR-Nonce`, and optional `X-DBR-Proof`, minted at
  `POST /v1/security/bootstrap`. A browser/bot gate, not an identity.
- **Supabase Bearer** (`supabaseBearer`): a signed-in session token on operations
  marked `x-databallr-permission: user`. A personal key is accepted there too.
- **Service API key** (`apiKey`): `X-API-Key` on routes that set the staged
  `REQUIRE_API_KEY` gate. Not a personal key.

## Conventions

- **Canonical names** live under `/v1`. A legacy `/api/...` path names its
  canonical in `x-databallr-alias-of`; the canonical lists those names in
  `x-databallr-aliases`. Keys cannot call the legacy names.
- **Scope** is `x-databallr-api-key-scope`: the data scope a key needs, or
  `null` when no key can call the operation.
- **Runtime** is `x-databallr-runtime`, always `worker` on this page. Same
  value as the `X-Databallr-Runtime` response header.
- **SixRings games** whose live copy is on `https://sixrings-api.databallr.com` carry `x-canonical-origin`. The copy documented here is the rollback.
- **Season type** is the `season_type` query parameter where a route reads one.
- Elevated, unknown-permission, and `/internal` operations are omitted.
